reason: Lahmu is the archetypal threshold guardian — the hairy protective spirit posted at temple and palace gates to turn back hostile forces and pollution.
His cult image frames doorways, gates, and thresholds; the guarded entrance is a foundational unit of sacred and defensive architecture.
The figure survives only in cuneiform ritual texts, seal impressions, and glazed reliefs; reconstructing Lahmu is an exercise in Near Eastern philology and archaeology.
Clay apotropaic figurines, bronze attachments, and glazed brick reliefs of Lahmu were manufactured as protective craft objects.
